title: Brent Interview — Group & Structure (quiz)
description: Broadview Holding's ownership, clusters, companies, hubs, Broadview One and the Broadview Business System. Practice + multiple-choice quiz; every card carries 5–6 distractors.

cards.front: Who ultimately owns Broadview Holding B.V.?
cards.back: Broadview belongs to the HAL group: HAL Investments holds ~97.4%; the ultimate parent is HAL Trust (Hamilton, Bermuda), listed in Amsterdam as HAL. This explains the long-term, decentralised philosophy and the €518m of shareholder loans on Broadview's balance sheet.
cards.quizAnswer: The HAL group — HAL Investments ~97%, ultimate parent HAL Trust, Amsterdam-listed.
distractors: A consortium of the founding families of Formica and Trespa.
Private-equity fund CVC Capital Partners via a 2019 buyout.
The Dutch state investment vehicle Invest-NL with minority partners.
It is independently listed on Euronext Amsterdam with dispersed ownership.
Westag AG, its German subsidiary, through a reverse holding structure.
A management buy-out led by CEO Matthijs Schoten in 2021.
cards.hint: Think Dutch listed investment company, Bermuda trust.

cards.front: What does Trespa make and where is it based?
cards.back: Weert, Netherlands. High-quality panels for exterior façade cladding and scientific/laboratory surfaces — functional as well as aesthetic. Exposure: commercial construction and renovation cycles; 2025 saw façade-cladding softness.
cards.quizAnswer: Weert, NL — façade cladding and laboratory/scientific surface panels.
distractors: Bra, Italy — decorative interior surfaces and the FENIX brand.

cards.front: What is Arpa Industriale known for, and what is FENIX?
cards.back: Arpa (Bra, Italy) makes decorative interior panels and surfaces; FENIX is its innovative interior-material brand (matt, soft-touch, anti-fingerprint, thermally repairable). Arpa's Bloom technology uses lignin to reduce fossil phenol in the core resin; FENIX NTX (Jun 2026) is up to 90% bio-based. Arpa and Formica Europe are now run together as Broadview Materials Europe.
cards.quizAnswer: Bra, Italy — decorative interior surfaces; FENIX is its innovative material brand.
distractors: Bra, Italy — exterior façade cladding; FENIX is its coating plant.

cards.back: The strategy to run the Materials companies as one business: product and customer perspective over legacy-company perspective; customers get access to the complete group portfolio; shared manufacturing, procurement, R&D, design, data and KPIs. Evidence: €117m intercompany Materials sales and growing; Valencia volumes moved to other plants; Arpa + Formica Europe = Broadview Materials Europe; Spanish commercial activities consolidated.
cards.quizAnswer: Running the Materials companies as one business — product/customer view over legacy-company view.
distractors: A single ERP system rolled out to all Broadview companies in 2025.
Merging the Materials and Energy clusters under one CEO.
A rebranding of every subsidiary under the Broadview name.
A cost-cutting programme targeting €100m savings by 2027.
A customer-loyalty scheme shared across Formica and Westag.

cards.front: What are the four dimensions of the Broadview Business System?
cards.back: Control non-business risk; grow the business; maximise the contribution of sales growth; have the right people. Budgets carry financial targets plus specific targets on each dimension. Umbrella: long-term orientation — companies should be 'the reference in their industry… still relevant decades from now'.
cards.quizAnswer: Control non-business risk; grow; maximise contribution of growth; the right people.
distractors: Cut costs; raise prices; reduce headcount; centralise purchasing.
Customer, process, learning and financial perspectives of a balanced scorecard.
Safety, quality, delivery and cost — the classic lean dashboard.
Grow revenue; expand margins; generate cash; return capital to HAL.
Innovate; digitalise; decarbonise; diversify geographically.

cards.front: What does Broadview mean by 'non-business risk'?
cards.back: Safety, compliance, reporting integrity, environmental and similar risks — a licence to operate, to be controlled rather than traded for commercial upside. Slogan: 'Find risks before they find you or your colleagues'. 2025: 46 accidents (51), 190 incidents (276); Westag had the most lost-time accidents (16).
cards.quizAnswer: Safety, compliance, reporting and similar risks that must be controlled, never traded for upside.
distractors: Macroeconomic and currency risks that the holding hedges centrally.
